meaning: a quality and limitation label carried with every figure. A caveat rendered as part of the headline rather than a footnote.

label: a reference corpus of deliberately hard cases

label: a public register with a revision history
meaning: a public register with a revision history. A record designed so that alteration is visible rather than possible.

label: a registry service that mints and resolves identifiers
meaning: a registry service that mints and resolves identifiers. A service whose whole job is to hand out identifiers and answer questions about them.

label: a controlled environment for practising a real task
meaning: a controlled environment for practising a real task. A place where the real task can be attempted without the real consequence.

label: a retrofit kit for equipment already installed

label: a multi-operator journey or logistics plan
meaning: a multi-operator journey or logistics plan. One plan that crosses parties who do not coordinate.

label: a booking and allocation arrangement for shared capacity
meaning: a booking and allocation arrangement for shared capacity. An allocation whose rules are published before the demand arrives.

meaning: a low-cost sensing kit with its calibration procedure. Instrumentation cheap enough to deploy widely and honest about its error.

meaning: a settlement mechanism with compensating actions. An exchange arrangement in which mistakes are corrected forward, not undone.

label: a wayfinding or signage system
meaning: a wayfinding or signage system. Physical information placed where the decision is made.

label: a simulator for rehearsing a decision before it is real
meaning: a simulator for rehearsing a decision before it is real. A place to be wrong cheaply.

label: a spare-parts and availability plan
meaning: a spare-parts and availability plan. A commitment about the future obtainability of a part.

label: a generator that produces a per-case statement
meaning: a generator that produces a per-case statement. A generator taking one case's records and emitting the statement that case needs.

label: a template kit with one fully filled worked example
meaning: a template kit with one fully filled worked example. Templates plus the completed example that shows what belongs in the blanks.

label: a test rig that measures a stated property
meaning: a test rig that measures a stated property. Apparatus that turns a claim into a measurement with a stated tolerance.

meaning: a short course with an assessment against criteria. Training that ends in a demonstration, not attendance.

meaning: a validator that reports per-record verdicts with reasons. A checker whose output explains the verdict rather than only stating it.

meaning: a printed wall chart for one specific setting. A single sheet that removes a choice rather than presenting all of them.

meaning: a complete worked reference example. One real case, done properly, published so others can adapt it.

label: an archive, library or collection
meaning: an archive, library or collection. Material held for a future nobody can specify.

label: a laboratory bench
meaning: a laboratory bench. One working surface, one operator, one method at a time.

meaning: a whole building. One structure with a design intent and an operating reality.

label: a single room or zone
meaning: a single room or zone. The scale at which comfort, safety and use are actually experienced.

label: a camp or informal settlement
meaning: a camp or informal settlement. People living where services were never planned.

label: a campus, estate or portfolio
meaning: a campus, estate or portfolio. Many buildings under one operator with inconsistent records.

label: a river catchment
meaning: a river catchment. A hydrological unit that ignores administrative boundaries.

label: bench-scale cell or tissue culture
meaning: bench-scale cell or tissue culture. Living material kept alive on a bench for a defined period.

label: a city
meaning: a city. One authority, many operators, and everybody's daily life.

label: a classroom or cohort
meaning: a classroom or cohort. Thirty different starting points and one timetable.

label: a voluntary community group
meaning: a voluntary community group. Commitment without budget, continuity without contracts.

label: a construction site
meaning: a construction site. A place that is different every week and dangerous every day.

label: a cooperative or member association
meaning: a cooperative or member association. Members who are also owners and also customers.

label: a court, tribunal or hearing
meaning: a court, tribunal or hearing. A forum where the record is the decision.

label: a cross-border arrangement
meaning: a cross-border arrangement. Two or more legal systems that must interoperate anyway.

label: a data centre or compute cluster
meaning: a data centre or compute cluster. Physical infrastructure people treat as abstract.

label: a department within an organisation
meaning: a department within an organisation. Enough people that process replaces memory.

label: an extended family or care network
meaning: an extended family or care network. People bound by obligation rather than contract.

label: a whole plant
meaning: a whole plant. Many lines, shared services and one site boundary.

label: a whole farm or holding
meaning: a whole farm or holding. One enterprise on land, with everything that implies.

label: a field plot or trial site
meaning: a field plot or trial site. A bounded piece of ground under a controlled treatment.

label: a fleet of vehicles
meaning: a fleet of vehicles. Many moving things allocated centrally.

label: a forest stand or plantation block
meaning: a forest stand or plantation block. Trees managed together on a decadal cycle.

label: a global network of independent participants
meaning: a global network of independent participants. No centre, many implementations, one specification.

label: a herd, flock, apiary or pen
meaning: a herd, flock, apiary or pen. A managed group of animals treated as one unit and many individuals.

meaning: a hospital or health system. Many services that must join up around one person.

label: one household
meaning: one household. An organisation with no organisation.

label: a single instrument or sensor station
meaning: a single instrument or sensor station. One device whose readings other things depend on.

label: a commercial or institutional kitchen
meaning: a commercial or institutional kitchen. A production space with a legal safety regime and no slack.

label: a large organisation
meaning: a large organisation. Many parts that must agree without meeting.

label: a machine cell on a shop floor
meaning: a machine cell on a shop floor. A few machines and the people who set them.

label: a market of many buyers and sellers
meaning: a market of many buyers and sellers. No party can instruct another and all of them respond to price.

label: a migratory range across jurisdictions
meaning: a migratory range across jurisdictions. A population whose range no single authority covers.

label: a mine site and its immediate surroundings
meaning: a mine site and its immediate surroundings. An operation whose consequences extend past its fence.

label: molecular and sub-cellular scale
meaning: molecular and sub-cellular scale. Structures and reactions below the level of a whole cell.

label: a multi-agency arrangement
meaning: a multi-agency arrangement. Several bodies, one person's problem.

label: a national jurisdiction
meaning: a national jurisdiction. One legal system, one statistical frame, many exceptions.

label: a neighbourhood
meaning: a neighbourhood. Small enough to know, large enough to disagree.

label: an observatory, orbit or remote-sensing programme
meaning: an observatory, orbit or remote-sensing programme. Instruments nobody can reach once deployed.

label: one person
meaning: one person. The scale at which everything is either usable or not.

label: a water or gas distribution network
meaning: a water or gas distribution network. Buried infrastructure known mostly by inference.

label: a port or freight terminal
meaning: a port or freight terminal. A place where custody changes hands under time pressure.

label: a production line
meaning: a production line. A sequence where every station waits for the one before.

label: a protocol with many independent implementations
meaning: a protocol with many independent implementations. A specification whose users cannot be instructed.

label: a reef, wetland or habitat patch
meaning: a reef, wetland or habitat patch. A place defined by what lives in it.

label: a sub-national region
meaning: a sub-national region. The level at which national rules meet local conditions.

label: a small team
meaning: a small team. Few enough people that coordination is conversation.

label: a small or medium enterprise
meaning: a small or medium enterprise. One organisation without specialist functions.

label: a running software service
meaning: a running software service. Something that must keep answering while it is being changed.

label: a single organism or specimen
meaning: a single organism or specimen. One individual, followed or examined.

label: a stage, hall or venue
meaning: a stage, hall or venue. A space that exists for one event at a time.

label: a street or block
meaning: a street or block. Where public space meets private frontage.

label: an electrical substation and its feeders
meaning: an electrical substation and its feeders. A node where the network's state becomes local and physical.

label: a multi-tier supply chain
meaning: a multi-tier supply chain. Parties who know their neighbours and not the chain.

label: a single vehicle or vessel
meaning: a single vehicle or vessel. One moving thing with its own state and log.

label: a ward, clinic or practice
meaning: a ward, clinic or practice. Where care is delivered and records are made in the gaps.

label: a repair workshop or maker bench
meaning: a repair workshop or maker bench. A place where one broken thing is dealt with at a time.

label: conditional decision gate
meaning: conditional decision gate. The target part runs only when a stated predicate over the source's result holds. Transfers: a verdict and the values it was computed from. Changes: the target becomes optional rather than unconditional. Shares: None.

label: one part sets a limit the other must respect
meaning: one part sets a limit the other must respect. The source publishes an operating envelope; the target must stay inside it and say what it does at the edge. Transfers: a limit value with a unit and a validity period. Changes: the target's admissible operating range narrows. Shares: the limit value.

label: several parts produce a coordinated result
meaning: several parts produce a coordinated result. Two or more parts jointly deliver an outcome that none of them delivers alone. Transfers: commitments and status about a joint outcome. Changes: a joint deliverable becomes attributable to the set rather than to one part. Shares: the joint outcome.

label: authority or custody passes to another part
meaning: authority or custody passes to another part. A scoped, expiring authority (or custody of a thing and its obligations) moves between parts. Transfers: an authorisation with a scope and an expiry, or custody of an entity. Changes: who may act, and who answers for the action. Shares: the accountability for the delegated act.

label: a product becomes a component of another product
meaning: a product becomes a component of another product. A complete deliverable is carried inside a larger deliverable and keeps its own acceptance. Transfers: the whole embedded product together with its own acceptance conditions. Changes: the larger product inherits the smaller one's obligations. Shares: the embedded product's identity.

label: a generator or configurator produces a further product
meaning: a generator or configurator produces a further product. One part is a generator; the other is a concrete product it must actually emit. Transfers: a configuration and the emitted artefact. Changes: the emitted product exists and must itself be acceptable. Shares: the generator's rule set.

label: feedback, revision and recovery
meaning: feedback, revision and recovery. An observation of the target's behaviour revises the source, within a bounded number of cycles. Transfers: a measured discrepancy and a revision instruction. Changes: an earlier part is revised after it was thought finished. Shares: None.

label: provides an input needed by another part
meaning: provides an input needed by another part. The source part produces a quantity of something the target part cannot start without. Transfers: a quantity of material, data, signal, credential or funds, with a unit. Changes: the target's prerequisite set becomes satisfiable. Shares: None.

label: shares a resource or an identity
meaning: shares a resource or an identity. Parts draw on one bounded pool, or refer to one entity by one identifier. Transfers: nothing; it establishes that two parts are bound to the same pool or identifier. Changes: consumption by one part reduces what remains for the other, or a rename in one breaks the other. Shares: a capacity pool or an entity identifier.

label: interaction repeated over time
meaning: interaction repeated over time. Two parts exchange on a stated cadence rather than once. Transfers: a repeated exchange on a cadence, each instance dated. Changes: state becomes perishable and must be refreshed. Shares: a clock.

label: RT-AUTHORITY
meaning: {part} shall act only within the authority declared by {authority} and shall stop at its expiry.

label: RT-CAPACITY-RESPECTED
meaning: {part} shall draw no more than its allocated {amount} {unit} from pool {pool_id}.

label: RT-COMPENSATE
meaning: Where {part} performs an irreversible step, it shall name the compensating action or state that none exists.

label: RT-DEADLINE
meaning: {part} shall be complete by day {day} of the case window.

label: RT-DEGRADE
meaning: On loss of {what}, {part} shall enter the declared safe state rather than continue on stale values.

label: RT-EMIT-CONCRETE
meaning: {part} shall emit at least one concrete product, not only a description of what it could emit.

label: RT-FIXTURE-LABEL
meaning: {part} shall label every synthetic fixture as hypothetical wherever it is displayed.

label: RT-IDENTITY-STABLE
meaning: {part} shall refer to {entity} by the identifier minted for it and by no other.

label: RT-INHERIT
meaning: {part} shall preserve the acceptance conditions of the product embedded within it.

label: RT-INPUT-PRESENT
meaning: {part} shall not begin before {what} is present in the stated form and quantity.

label: RT-JOINT-OUTCOME
meaning: {part} shall contribute the named share of the joint outcome {outcome}.

label: RT-JUDGMENT
meaning: {part} shall record who made each judgment call and against which written criterion.

label: RT-LIMIT-RESPECT
meaning: {part} shall stay within the limit of {amount} {unit} published by {source} and shall declare its behaviour at the limit.

label: RT-METHOD-CITED
meaning: Every value {part} reports shall cite the method and version that produced it.

label: RT-PRIVACY
meaning: {part} shall not publish an identifier that resolves to a named individual.

label: RT-RECORD-DISAGREEMENT
meaning: Where parties disagree, {part} shall retain both accounts rather than resolve them silently.

label: RT-RESUME
meaning: {part} shall resume from its partial state without discarding completed work.

label: RT-REVOCATION
meaning: {part} shall cease using {what} within the stated interval after the authorisation is withdrawn.

label: RT-STALENESS
meaning: {part} shall render the age of {what} and mark it stale beyond {bound} {unit}.

label: RT-TRACE
meaning: Every figure {part} publishes shall be traceable to the source record it came from.

label: RT-UNIT-CARRIED
meaning: Every quantity {part} emits shall carry a unit from the declared unit table.

label: RT-VERSION-STAMP
meaning: {part} shall stamp its output with the version of the rules applied.

label: CT-ACCEPTANCE_COVER
meaning: Every required deliverable carries at least one acceptance condition.

label: CT-ACYCLIC
meaning: Directed dependency relationships form no cycle; revision cycles are permitted only through RK-FEEDBACK with a bound.

label: CT-AUTHORITY_SCOPED
meaning: Any delegated authority carries a named scope and an expiry day within the case window.

label: CT-CAPACITY_BOUND
meaning: Total draw on shared pool {pool_id} ({resource}) across all parts must not exceed {capacity} {unit}.

label: CT-DEPTH_BOUND
meaning: Composition depth must not exceed {max_depth}, so recursive construction terminates.

label: CT-DIMENSION_MATCH
meaning: A quantity transferred between two parts must be expressed in the dimension the receiving part expects.

label: CT-GENERATOR_EMITS
meaning: A generator part must be paired with at least one concrete emitted product by an RK-EMIT relationship.

label: CT-HYPOTHETICAL_LABELLED
meaning: Every synthetic fixture is labelled hypothetical and is never presented as an observed record.

label: CT-IDENTITY_UNIQUE
meaning: Each entity identifier in this case denotes exactly one entity of one declared type.

label: CT-JUDGMENT_RECORDED
meaning: Each judgment call is recorded with the criteria applied and the person who applied them.

label: CT-LANGUAGE_PARITY
meaning: Where several working languages apply, every language version carries the same obligations.

label: CT-PII_MINIMISED
meaning: Personal identifiers are excluded from any published artefact of this case.

label: CT-PREREQ_CLOSED
meaning: Every prerequisite declared by a part is met by a concrete input, an inbound relationship, or a recorded assumption.

label: CT-REGIME_ADMISSIBLE
meaning: Every ingredient used must declare the regime of the part that uses it.

label: CT-REVERSIBILITY_DECLARED
meaning: Each irreversible step names the compensating action available after it, or states that none exists.

label: CT-SAFETY_INTERLOCK
meaning: The unsafe action is made impossible by construction rather than discouraged by instruction.

label: CT-SCHEDULE_FEASIBLE
meaning: Every part must finish by day {deadline_day} given its duration and the precedences declared.

label: CT-SITUATION_ADMISSIBLE
meaning: Every ingredient used must declare at least one of the case's situation tags.

label: CT-STALENESS_BOUND
meaning: Repeated exchanges declare a staleness bound and the rendering used once it is exceeded.

label: CT-UNIT_DECLARED
meaning: Every transferred quantity carries a unit drawn from the dictionary unit table.

label: CT-VERSION_STAMPED
meaning: Outputs derived from versioned rules carry the version of the rules that produced them.

label: S-AUDIT
meaning: An external party can compel evidence about what was done.

label: S-COLLABORATIVE
meaning: Independent parties must act together to get any result.

label: S-CONCURRENT
meaning: Several actors act on one object at the same time.

label: S-CRISIS
meaning: An emergency in which the normal process cannot be followed.

label: S-DISPUTE
meaning: Parties disagree about facts, entitlement or attribution.

label: S-DIVIDED-AUTHORITY
meaning: Approval sits with one body and delivery with another.

label: S-HANDOVER
meaning: Custody, duty or knowledge passes between parties.

label: S-INTERRUPTED
meaning: The work is interrupted and must resume from a partial state.

label: S-IRREVERSIBLE
meaning: At least one step cannot be undone once taken.

label: S-LEARNING
meaning: Someone must reach competence, not merely receive information.

label: S-LONG-HORIZON
meaning: The horizon exceeds the organisation's own memory.

label: S-LOW-CAPACITY
meaning: The party who must act lacks tooling, staff or expertise.

label: S-MAINTENANCE
meaning: The purpose is keeping something already built working.

label: S-MULTILINGUAL
meaning: Several working languages must carry the same obligations.

label: S-PEAK
meaning: Demand or contention at its seasonal or daily peak.

label: S-PRIVACY-SENSITIVE
meaning: Disclosure could harm an identifiable person.

label: S-PUBLIC-FACING
meaning: Members of the public encounter the result directly.

label: S-REMOTE
meaning: Work happens far from support, often without connectivity.

label: S-ROUTINE
meaning: Steady routine operation with known inputs.

label: S-SAFETY-CRITICAL
meaning: A foreseeable failure injures people or destroys value.

label: S-SCARCITY
meaning: A resource needed by several parts is genuinely short.

label: S-SEASONAL
meaning: A short window governs when the work is possible at all.

label: S-SOLO
meaning: One person or household acts alone, without an organisation.

label: S-STARTUP
meaning: A new arrangement with no operating history to learn from.

label: S-TIME-BOUNDED
meaning: A bounded response time decides whether the result is useful at all.

label: S-UNCERTAIN-EVIDENCE
meaning: The evidence is noisy, missing, contested or assumed.

label: S-VERSION-CHANGE
meaning: A definition, schema or rule changes on a schedule.
